{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that participants would show a preference for joint action over individual action, even when the joint action is instrumentally disadvantageous due to coordination costs.",
  "design": "mixed, with task mode (alone vs. together) as a within-subject factor and number of boxes (4, 8, 12) as a within-subject factor.",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "The choice between performing a task alone (clearing all items) or together with a partner (splitting items and requiring synchronous tapping).",
  "outcome_measure": "The proportion of trials in which the decision-maker chose to perform the task together.",
  "population_and_setting": "Adult participants recruited in pairs, tested in a laboratory setting using a touchscreen-based game.",
  "sample_size_total": 40,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Participants were recruited in pairs and received monetary compensation independent of their task performance.",
  "analysis_plan": "A one-sample t-test (or Wilcoxon signed-rank test) comparing the average proportion of together choices against chance level (0.5).",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants were instructed not to communicate. The task involved clearing boxes on a touchscreen. In together trials, participants had to tap synchronously on the same items. The decision-maker's score was based on the number of boxes cleared. Trials exceeding 3 standard deviations from the mean were excluded."
}
